text:
maya: Kicking off the region-by-region rollout for v2.3.1 — US -> EU -> APAC. Change window starts 09:00 PT. I’m pinning traffic to v2.3.1 in the canary slice for the first 20m. Can ops/SRE confirm warm pools and surge cushion?

deploy-bot: @channel deploy job queued: release=v2.3.1 id=deploy-1799999999. Canary slice: 3% traffic. Auto-fallback rules: if error_rate > 0.5% for 5m OR tail-latency_p95 increases by >200ms, deploybot will halt and @maya notified.

tom: US warm pool is green. Reserved GPUs: 32 (equiv ~1.6k rps for our gen2 models). Cushion: +20% on top of expected. EU warm pool warming now, expected to hit target in ~12m. APAC needs an extra warmup step, ETA 30m.

anika: Running the preflight smoke now — small traffic sweep to canary (curl against canary route). No regressions on the eval set so far. Latency P95 baseline ~110ms US. I pushed a short checklist in #eng-releases-docs (link).

james: FYI product: release notes include the telemetry fix (avoids duplicate traces), improved batching heuristics, and a small change to tokenizer config. No user-facing API changes.

maya: Good. Tom, if EU falls short of cushion we keep EU pinned at 0 traffic until we can backfill warm pool? Also confirm commit for pinned variant (sha: a1b2c3d4).

tom: Correct — EU will be soft-pinned to previous version if cushion < +10% after warmup. Confirmed variant sha a1b2c3d4 for v2.3.1. I'll put a holdpoint at EU canary completion.

ops-bot: Preflight checks: 
- infra quota ok: US: OK, EU: OK (pending warmup), APAC: WARN (low warm pool)
- rate-limits validated
- monitoring hooks attached (datadog, otel)

anika: Quick note on rollback criteria: if user-facing errors spike OR automated eval set F1 drops by >3 points, we roll back the canary to v2.3.0 and run snapshot diffs. Keep evaluation run id handy: eval-2026-03-21-17.

maya: Plan: start US canary 09:00, observe 20m. If good, roll 25% to US and start EU canary warmup. EU observation window 30m. Only after EU stable do we begin APAC warmup. We will not cross-start EU and APAC warmups in parallel because APAC warmup needs on-prem GPUs.

tom: Understood. I'll monitor thermal metrics and OOMs. If thermal throttling > 10% for 10m we pause and backfill to dedicated reserve.

deploy-bot: Action log:
```
[09:00:00] deploy-1799999999 start canary US (3%) -> v2.3.1
[09:05:00] smoke sweep OK (0.02% err)
[09:18:00] latency p95 +12ms (within threshold)
[09:20:00] canary holdpoint reached, awaiting manual ACK
```

maya: ACKing canary holdpoint. Proceed to US 25% roll at 09:25. Tom, please confirm metrics dashboard link and alerts are green before the 25% bump.

tom: dashboards all green: https://dd/redwood/dash/deploy-1799999999. Alerts: none firing. Ready for 25%. :thumbsup:

anika: One post-deploy sanity: run `python tools/consume_test_prompts.py --env=prod --slice=us --count=500` and check top-5 hallucination rate. Report back in thread.

maya: Also leaving a rollback window until 11:00 PT where we can safely unwind traffic without cross-region inconsistencies. If we hit rollback after that we'll need a staged unwind.

james: Noted for customers — we’ll publish brief status in release-notes channel when EU canary is green. Keep messaging tight.

deploy-bot: Update: US 25% roll started at [09:25]. Monitoring autoscaling and prefix cache hit-rates.

anika: Sanity run results: 500 prompts consumed, hallucination rate 0.8% (baseline 0.9%) — looks stable.

tom: EU warm pool reached target. Starting EU canary (3%) now. APAC warmup queued behind EU.

maya: Thanks everyone. If anyone sees an anomalous spike ping @oncall immediately and call out region in caps. We'll reconvene in 45m if any holdpoints trip.

ops-bot: Reminder: change window metadata attached to this thread. Retention: 72h for ops traces.

maya: closing the loop here — please call rollback explicitly in thread if trigger conditions met. Otherwise I’ll file the rollout complete note once APAC finishes. :white_check_mark:
